sourceIssues.printed: Corollary 1.1.15 takes any connected reductive G over Q_p, a Q_p-rational Levi M, a minuscule μ: G_m → M, and [b_M] ∈ B(M)_b with ([b_M], {μ}) G-admissible. It claims some w ∈ W(G, M) := N_G(M)/M makes ([b_M], {w·μ}) M-admissible. The proof invokes (1.1.13) for w* ∈ W(G*, M*) making ([b_{M*}], {w*·μ*}) M*-admissible.
sourceIssues.correction: Use the absolute geometric Weyl group W(G,T) for a maximal torus T of M containing a representative of μ, with compatible choices under the inner twisting, rather than N_G(M)/M. Equivalently, some G(Q̄_p)-conjugate μ′ of μ factoring through T makes ([b_M], {μ′}) M-admissible. No Q_p-rationality of μ or of a chosen Weyl representative is asserted.
sourceIssues.reason: The printed statement fails already for split G. Take G = GL_3, M = GL_1 × GL_2 (blocks of sizes 1 and 2), μ = (0,1,0) and b_M = diag(p,1,1), which is basic in M. Then ([b_M], {μ}) is G-admissible: its Newton point (1,0,0) equals the dominant μ̄, and both have κ_G = 1. But κ_M(b_M) = (1,0), while κ_M(μ) = (0,1). Since the blocks have different sizes, N_G(M) = M, so W(G, M) is trivial and no w in it helps. The permutation of the first two coordinates, in W(G, T) = S_3, does. The proof transports to the quasi-split inner form and applies Proposition 1.1.13. That proposition gives w* in the absolute Weyl group W(G*, T*), not in N_{G*}(M*)/M*, so the proof establishes the corrected statement. The only use is in the proof of Corollary 1.1.17, p.13, for G not necessarily quasi-split. It cites "Lemma 1.1.13" (the quasi-split Proposition 1.1.13) in the form w ∈ W(G, T). The corrected Corollary 1.1.15 is exactly what that step needs, so this particular downstream step is repaired; this is not a verification of every later result. Checked on the page images. Noted by the extraction (source discrepancy 2, items N29 and N32), which also verified the Weyl-group computation by machine.

sourceIssues.printed: The source sets G′ = G × T, V′ = V ⊕ V and X′ = X × {h_T}, claiming (G′, X′) ↪ (G_{V′}, H_{V′}). Restriction of I_{s′_0} to A_T is said to give I_{s′_0} → T, hence I_{s′_0} → T → G^ab. It invokes Corollary 2.1.9 for surjectivity of I_{s′_0} → I_{s_0} and deduces that I_{s′_0} → G^ab factors through I_{s_0}, citing this factorization over Q_ℓ for every ℓ ≠ p.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace G′=G×T by G′=G×_{G^ab}T. This is a connected reductive central-torus extension of G: its kernel is 1×(T∩G^der). The similitude character factors through G^ab, so the two blocks have equal multipliers. Since h^ab is constant on X, X×{h_T} factors through G′. After constructing the lift and its CM factor as in the proof, Corollary 2.1.9 identifies the ℓ-adic groups with Frobenius centralizers. Their projection is surjective and its kernel lies in 1×(T∩G^der), which maps trivially to G^ab. Faithfully flat descent then gives I_s→G^ab. The written proof must include this kernel argument; surjectivity alone is insufficient.
sourceIssues.reason: The direct-product construction is false as written, not merely an unexplained descent: already for G=GSp_2 and a CM maximal torus T, (1,2·1)∈G×T scales the two blocks of ψ⊕ψ by 1 and 4. Thus it is not a symplectic similitude. Independently of that failed Shimura construction, on the proposed direct-product group the composite G×T→T→G^ab is nontrivial on the kernel 1×T of projection to G, so it cannot descend. The original errata's unconditional claim about I_{s′} is replaced by this group-level obstruction, since the proposed Shimura embedding has already failed. In the repaired fibre product, projection to G has central torus kernel, so geometric Frobenius centralizers surject: after splitting off the connected center up to isogeny, centralizing a semisimple element is unchanged on the derived factor. Corollary 2.1.9 then gives surjectivity on the I-groups; over Q_ℓ the kernel is killed by T→G^ab, hence over Q as well. Read Lemma 2.2.8, Corollary 2.1.9 and the preceding lifting construction. This repairs the identified local construction/descent; it is not a global certification of Proposition 2.2.2, whose preceding construction has the related E13 defect.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 2.2.11 takes an irreducible finite-type k-scheme S, a Zariski dense Γ ⊂ S(k), a finite subgroup W ⊂ Aut_k S, and σ ∈ Aut_k S. If each γ ∈ Γ admits some w ∈ W with w(γ) = σ(γ), it concludes σ = w for one w ∈ W.
sourceIssues.correction: Assume S is reduced and separated over k. Among the finitely many sets Γ_w one is dense by irreducibility. The equalizer of σ and that w is a closed subscheme by separatedness; its defining ideal vanishes at every point of S and is therefore zero by reducedness. Hence σ=w.
sourceIssues.reason: Take k=Q and W={1}. On S=Spec Q[ε]/(ε²), ε↦2ε is a nonidentity automorphism fixing the unique, dense rational point. Separately, the reduced affine line with doubled origin over Q is irreducible and of finite type, and exchanging its origins fixes the dense set Q×. This supplies the missing infinite-field condition in the original second example. Thus the lemma as stated is false and affects a stated result, even though its application on p.30 is to a smooth affine torus and satisfies both added hypotheses. Independently checked the p.29 image, the proof and the application. The extraction subsequently recorded the same reach correction; this checkpoint supplies it in the errata file too.

sourceIssues.printed: The source takes a flat normal W-scheme S of finite type, a relative Cartier divisor D ⊂ S, and the inclusion j : U = D − S ↪ S. It equips S with the log structure j_*O_U.
sourceIssues.correction: U = S − D, and S carries the divisorial log structure O_S ∩ j_*O_U^× → O_S.
sourceIssues.reason: D⊂S, so D−S is empty and cannot be the intended open complement on which the abelian scheme lives. For U=S−D, the intended log structure is the multiplicative monoid of regular functions invertible on U. The defect in j_*O_U is not that it is a sheaf of rings (rings also have underlying multiplicative monoids). For S=Spec W[x] and D=(x), j_*O_U contains x^{-1}; a monoid map to O_S agreeing with the identity on U would force the nonunit x to be a unit. Intersecting O_S with j_*O_U^× fixes precisely that problem. Independently checked the p.37 image and A.2–A.3.

Replace the group by the identity component of the subgroup of G′×_{G^ad}G cut out by c′(g′)=c(g). The paired Hodge homomorphism has equal multipliers and factors through this subgroup. Recheck the subsequent lifting and centralizer arguments for this corrected group; the present checkpoint establishes the missing condition, not the full repaired proposition.
sourceIssues.reason: The fibre product over the adjoint group does not identify the central multipliers, and taking its identity component does not fix this. Test G′=G=GSp_2=GL_2 with the same Siegel datum and standard representation. The curve a↦(a·1,1) lies in the identity component of the fibre product over PGL_2. At a=2 its block-diagonal action scales ψ′ by 4 and ψ by 1, so it is not a similitude of their direct sum. These data satisfy the accommodating type-C setup (standard two-dimensional representation, with no proper nonzero invariant subspace). Hence the asserted embedding fails even in this basic allowed case. The equality-of-multipliers subgroup removes the obstruction; this is distinct from E5, where equality in all of G^ab is needed for descent. Independently read §2.2.7 pp.26–28 and the p.27 image. E13 avoids reusing E8–E12, which already identify different findings in the newer extraction.
